newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia urges Iranians to avoid haj rallies.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia urges Iranians to avoid haj rallies.

text.p: Saudi Arabia on Wednesday urged Iranian pilgrims to refrain from holding political rallies during the haj pilgrimage in the kingdom, an issue which has strained ties between the two Gulf powers for years.
"Iranian officials understand the matter and heed should be taken from the previous years," Saudi Interior Minister Prince Nayef told a news conference in Mecca.
"We hope that all pilgrims, not only the Iranians, will respect this sacred ritual and respect its security and the security of the kingdom of Saudi Arabia," he added.
Iranian state radio on Tuesday urged Moslems to stage a rally, called the "disavowal of infidels" ceremony, during haj to protest against Israel's policies in Jerusalem.

Political activities are banned by conservative Sunni Saudi Arabia during haj, but radical Shi'ite Iran says pilgrims should hold rallies to denounce Israel and the United States as enemies of Islam. The haj reaches its climax next week.
Prince Nayef said he did not believe rallies would take place at this year's haj.

The row between the Gulf's two richest oil countries over the political rallies has resurfaced before every haj since 1987, when 402 people, mostly Iranians, died in clashes with Saudi security forces. Iran boycotted haj for three years.
Saudi Arabia has said it would deal harshly with violators of a ban on political activity during haj.
To avoid direct confrontation with Saudi security, Iranian pilgrims in previous years staged rallies within Iran's haj compound in Mecca and Saudi forces did not interfere.
About two million Moslems -- half of them from outside Saudi Arabia -- are expected to perform this year's haj at Mecca, site of Islam's holiest shrine.
